evidence: pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both branches, so the flag lookup does nothing and the function always returns false. That makes the QueryTypeSQL case at reader.go:129-132 always return 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The claim is correct. The behavior itself is intended: this is the CVE-2024-9264 hard-disable, and pkg/expr/sql/db.go is a stub whose methods all return 'not implemented'. So nothing is broken at runtime. Still, the inverted variable name and identical branches make it look as if the feature flag re-enables SQL expressions, which could mislead a future maintainer. Replacing the body with `return false` plus a comment explaining the security disable (or inlining it) would be clearer. This is a readability fix, not a correctness bug.

The 80% docstring threshold is CodeRabbit's own generic check; the repository does not enforce it. .golangci.toml:295-309 turns off the stylecheck doc-comment rules (ST1000, ST1020, ST1021, each marked 'TODO: Enable'). The revive section (lines 9-12) configures no 'exported' rule, and golangci-lint excludes revive's exported-comment warnings by default. Nearby existing code also has no doc comments on exported identifiers, e.g. ExpressionQueryReader and NewExpressionQueryReader at pkg/expr/reader.go:35-43. The new undocumented functions are throwaway stubs in pkg/expr/sql/db.go:9-26 (DB, TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto, NewInMemoryDB) that just return 'not implemented'. The one new unexported helper, enableSqlExpressions, is covered by issue 0. Adding a comment there saying why SQL expressions are disabled would help, but a coverage percentage is not a valid review finding for this codebase.
